_about: The nightly's KIT: everything a machine that starts empty needs, beside the checkout, to build the site the laptop builds. Measured and argued in the cloud-move plan of 25 September 2026; read by cloud.py, and held to the build by preflight.

Paths are relative to the working folder, with / between folders. In a glob, * and ? stay inside one folder and ** crosses any number of them. Every entry must match something unless it says optional.

owner says who writes a file. A 'night' file is the nightly's own: the laptop sends it once, with seed-kit, and never over the night's copy after that. A 'laptop' file is made by the laptop's jobs: the night reads it and never sends it back. One writer per file, because two is how the older copy wins.

state is the handful of small files a night must remember. On a machine they live under archive/, the project's one place for small state (refused.json, census.json); in the bucket they live under state/. backup is the laptop's copy of everything git does not hold, less what it leaves out and why. never is what no command sends anywhere.

kit.what: The day's files, where the nightly installs them: the twelve of snapshot_gencourt.py's fourteen that git does not track. GeneralCodes.txt and BodyStatusCodes.txt arrive with the checkout.
Each day's copy of those files: what gc_changes.py compares the night's with.
Past terms' dockets, fetched and dumped: narrate_archive.py, build_manifest.py and extract_chapters.py read them.
The database views the build reads, of the 31 in the dump.

The study and statutory committees -- their details, meetings and members, and the dump's temporary view of them -- and the dump's manifest, whose StatStudMeetings date the calendar reads. The night's study-committee refresh swaps all four views in whole.
Who sits on each committee, who chairs it, and the members who have left; the night's weekly job refreshes them.
The towns in each Senate district, which the build does not make.
Outputs a build reads before it rewrites them: build_all.CARRIED. Without last night's copy each one changes the site without anything failing.
The archived terms' manifests, one per term, from build_manifest.py --docket.
What the laptop's jobs make and the build reads.
The calendars' and journals' text: the .txt beside each PDF, not the PDF.
Times read off the recordings, and where each recording's captions stop: the caption job's answers, not the 20 GB of captions it read them from.
The licensed logo the build lays over the clipart. Private: never in the repository, allowed in the bucket and on the build machine. brand/licensed/, which it is drawn from, goes to the backup only.

The one file of last night's site a build reads before it rewrites it: build_pages.py counts the committees with a roster for the home page out of site/committees.json, which build_committees.py writes later in the same build. A build from the kit alone on 25 September differed from the laptop's in this and in two sitemap addresses, of 54,975 files; build_bill_pages.py has since listed those addresses whatever is on disk.

The night's new livestreams: the index rows the committed videos_*.csv do not carry. Their state is archive/livestreams.json, in the state list below. Optional: none exists before the first night that finds a livestream.

state.what: A refusal on file: nothing asks the General Court, from either machine, until a person clears it.
The last accepted build's counts and fingerprint, which nightly.py's gates compare with.
The night's verdict, for the morning.
What livestreams.py has seen and waits for, and what it read off recordings the laptop has not yet read. The night writes it; the laptop's --catch-up only reads it.
How far the reader reports have been pulled. A number, never a reader's words.

logs.what: What kit-up sends to logs/<date>/: the night's logs and its what-changed report, written since kit-down.

backup.what: Everything in the working folder that git does not track, except these.

leave_out.why: the repository itself, which GitHub holds, and the assistant's own state
cloud.py's own record of this machine, locks, and files half written
a night's log carries what the report pull printed, which can be a reader's own words; the About page promises those are gone within a week
the built site, remade from the kit and the code every night; --with-site sends it

never.what: Sent by no command: not in the kit, the state or the backup, whatever else matches.
